---
title: Fire Safety Briefing
minutes: 15
---
# Fire safety at ==Riverside Bakery==
Yearly staff briefing · ==October 2026==

::: notes
Welcome everyone and thank them for the time. Say that this briefing takes about 15 minutes, that it is required once a year, and that everyone signs the attendance list at the end. Ask people to keep their phones away until the quiz. Say that questions are welcome at any time; a briefing does not test anyone, it makes everyone safer.
:::

---
## Why we brief every year

- Bakeries work with ovens, fryers and flour dust every day
- Most kitchen fires start small and are put out in the first minute
- The law asks us to brief everyone once a year and keep a record

::: notes
Explain that this is not a formality. A kitchen fire grows fast, and the first minute decides whether it stays a small incident. Mention that the employer must brief every employee on fire safety at least once a year and when the work changes, and that the signed list proves we did it. Ask whether anyone has seen a kitchen fire before; let one or two people tell the story briefly.
:::

---
# What starts a fire here

Ovens, fat and dust

::: notes
Move on to the causes. Say that the next slides cover the three things that start most fires in a bakery, and what each of us does to prevent them.
:::

---
## The three usual causes

::: columns
### In the bakehouse
- Fat and oil overheating in fryers
- Flour dust near open flames
- Crumbs left in ovens and toasters
+++
### Everywhere
- Damaged cables and overloaded sockets
- Cleaning cloths on hot surfaces
- Blocked vents on fridges and proofers
:::

::: notes
Walk through both columns. For the fryer, say the thermostat must never be bypassed and the oil changed on schedule. For flour dust, point out that a cloud of fine flour can burn in a flash, so we sweep, never blow it off with compressed air. Ask each person to name one place in our shop where they have seen a risk like this.
:::

---
## When the alarm sounds

1. Stop work and switch off the machines you use
2. Leave by the nearest marked exit, never the lift
3. Help guests and new colleagues out
4. Meet at the assembly point: ==the car park across the street==

::: notes
Go through the steps slowly and in order. Stress that no one goes back for bags, coats or the till. The shift lead takes the attendance sheet for the day to the assembly point and counts everyone. Name the assembly point and point to it on the escape plan by the door.
:::

---
## Our escape routes

![Escape plan of the shop with exits and the assembly point](images/escape-plan.png)

::: notes
Point to the two exits on the plan and to the assembly point. Ask everyone to find the plan by the door on their way out today.
:::

---
## Which extinguisher for which fire

| Fire | Class | Use | Never |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paper, wood, cloth | A | Water or foam | |
| Fat and oil | F | Wet chemical, fire blanket | Water |
| Electrical | – | CO2 after switching off | Water |

::: notes
Show where each extinguisher hangs. The most important line is fat and oil: water on burning fat causes an explosion of burning oil. Use the wet chemical extinguisher or put the fire blanket over the pan and switch off the heat. Leave the blanket in place until the pan is cold.
:::

---
## Remember this

> Water on burning fat turns a small fire into a fireball. Cover it, switch off the heat, step back.

::: notes
Pause here and let the sentence sink in. Ask someone to repeat the three actions in their own words.
:::

---
## Question 1

Burning oil in the fryer. What do you do first?

- [ ] Pour water on it
- [x] Switch off the heat and cover it with the fire blanket
- [ ] Carry the pan outside

::: notes
Let people answer out loud before you reveal the answer. Explain why each wrong answer is dangerous: water makes the fat explode, and whoever carries a burning pan spills burning oil on themselves and others.
:::

---
## Question 2

The alarm sounds while you are serving a guest. Where do you go?

- [ ] Back to the bakehouse to switch off the oven
- [ ] Out through the kitchen door to the yard
- [x] Out of the nearest exit to the car park across the street

::: notes
The right answer is the assembly point. Switching off your own machine is fine if it takes a second, but nobody walks back into the building.
:::

---
## Questions and signatures

- Ask what is still unclear
- Hand out the quiz and the attendance list
- Next briefing: ==October 2027==

::: notes
Answer the open questions. Then hand out the quiz; give people ten minutes and go through the answers together. Finally everyone signs the attendance list, and you file it with the date of this briefing.
:::
